title: Cross-scale organisation of the atmospheric circulation: a falsification-grade research programme (Shroedinger, gen4)
description:
Falsification-grade research programme on the cross-scale organisation of the atmospheric circulation. This release supersedes v4.0 and records the outcome of five further preregistered phases (9-13), each with criteria frozen before the data were retrieved and every deviation logged.

What stands. The cross-scale envelope-coupling profile P - the spatial rank correlation between the activity maps of adjacent octave levels of the 850 hPa relative vorticity field - is a regional invariant: a season-, year- and ENSO-stable signature (p = 0.001 on held-out samples), not reducible to the semi-fractal level features or to symmetric cross-scale statistics. Its independence of the full power spectrum is conditional after the domain-geometry control (p = 0.10).

The observing-network confound is closed. The regional geography of P replicates in a free-running CMIP6 HighResMIP integration that assimilates no atmospheric observations (Spearman rho = 0.71 against an ERA5-to-ERA5 across-period ceiling of 0.93). The property belongs to the atmosphere, not to the observing system - the limitation that reanalysis-only studies cannot resolve.

What is retracted. The interpretation of the inter-level transfer asymmetry index A. The index remains a reproducible regional statistic (MERRA-2 rho = 0.93; free-running model rho = 0.90), but on synthetic fields where irrecoverability is known and swept it does not respond in either the spatial or the modal reading, while it tracks temporal persistence (Spearman 1.0 synthetic, +0.53 on real domains). A is a persistence statistic; the cause is methodological, the transfer operators being fitted over a sliding window.

Applied content: tested and not found. Three derived predictions were tested and failed - the rate of ensemble forecast error growth (NOAA GEFS), the level of analysis-time mesoscale error, and the mesoscale deficit of machine-learning weather models (WeatherBench 2). In all three, plain band variance was a stronger predictor than the descriptors. The AI-model result stands on its own: deterministic and ensemble-mean models lose 55-85 % of mesoscale variance at a five-day lead in the 200-800 km band, while a physical model and a single generative sample lose essentially none.

Contents. Fourteen frozen preregistered protocols with deviation logs; the full experiment catalogue with reconciliation statuses; per-region-window numerical results; the current manuscript (Russian) and its predecessors; and the complete catalogue of negative results.
notes: Supersedes release v4.0 (gen3). The gen3 branch is frozen; development continues on gen4.
